#3417. Nintendo's Black Friday Deals Are Actually Pretty Good

Black Friday is nearly upon us. From now through Cyber Monday, retailers and companies alike are offering deals and discounts on their wares. While I always keep an eye out for Nintendo deals offered by stores like Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart, it seems the company is offering its own discounts this year—and, surprisingly, they're actually pretty solid.

Last Thursday, Nintendo announced its Black Friday discounts. We've already seen Switch 2 sales ahead of the Black Friday season, but now, Nintendo has confirmed an official discount for the console.

Starting Nov. 22 through Dec. 5, you can pick up Nintendo's Switch 2 Mario Kart bundle for $499.99, down $50 from $549.99. That includes the console, a download of Mario Kart World, and a 90-day Nintendo Switch Online Individual Membership.

If you already have a Switch 2 console and/or Mario Kart World, you're not left out of the Black Friday deals here. From Nov. 22 through Nov. 29, Nintendo is also running discounts on several high-profile Switch and Switch 2 games:

Donkey Kong Bananza was one of Nintendo's launch titles for the Switch 2. And while it's been out for over a year, Donkey Kong's first 3D game is still among the best-reviewed titles on the console. Nintendo is taking $30 off the game's MSRP for this promotion.

Kirby Air Riders on Switch 2 is only the second installment in the series. The original launched all the way back on the GameCube, and while the title typically runs for $69.99, Nintendo is letting it go for $39.99.

Metroid Prime 4 arrived last year after an 18-year wait from Metroid Prime 3: Corruption. The game typically retails between $59.99 and $69.99 for a physical copy, but Nintendo is selling it for $39.99 during its early Black Friday promotion.

Super Mario Galaxy (both the original and the sequel) are beloved by fans. These titles originally launched on the Wii, and Nintendo rereleased both for the Switch. (The company offers a free upgrade to the Switch 2 edition.) Nintendo asks $69.99 for this combo, and while you can find it for under $60, you'll officially be able to pick it up for $39.99 before Black Friday.

Nintendo's latest Mario Party, Jamboree, has a Switch 2 edition with a rather staggering MSRP of $79.99. While it's the version of the game with the most features, it's also the most expensive. You'll be able to buy it for $39.99 for Black Friday, saving up to $40.

Nintendo rarely offers official discounts on some of its biggest titles, especially in this current era. In addition, Nintendo announced a sale on its digital store that runs from Nov. 19 through Dec. 2, though it didn't say which titles would be on sale. Just keep an eye on all these dates: The Switch 2 console promotion runs longer than the physical and digital games discounts, while the digital sale runs longer than the physical sale. Nintendo says that these discounts will be available "at select retailers," as well as its brick-and-mortar locations in New York and San Francisco. You can also buy the Switch 2 bundle through Nintendo's website.

It depends! Its Nintendo Switch 2 bundle deal runs from Nov. 22 through Dec. 5; the select games listed above will be on sale from Nov. 22 through Nov. 29; and digital titles will have discounts from Nov. 19 through Dec. 2.

While we don't know which digital titles will be discounted yet, we do know that physical copies of Donkey Kong Bananza, Kirby Air Riders, Metroid Prime 4: Beyond, Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2, and Super Mario Party: Jamboree will be on sale for $39.99 each.

Yes! The Switch 2 alone costs $499.99, so you essentially get the game for free. Mario Kart World is also one of the console's best multiplayer titles right now, so it makes sense to pick it up in this bundle.

#3416. Every Playable Video Game in GTA 6, Ranked Worst to Best

Why rob a bank when you can play Time Jackers?

Grand Theft Auto 6 is so big that it’s actually five games in one. Like previous games in the series, there are several games-within-the-game that you can play while hanging out in Leonida. These aren’t just quick arcade games that you can play for a few minutes, but full-on console games that are actually pretty fun in their own right.

It’s a playful meta joke from Rockstar, and I would be remiss not to play into it. Where there are games, there must be a video game website ranking those games in an arbitrary list. Here’s how the four games featured in GTA 6 stack up. Even if they aren’t all winners, they’re all at least high-effort jokes that deserve some praise.

As a parody of the kind of hunting games you find in dive bars, Bang For Your Buck is a pretty one-note gag. It’s an on-rails shooter where you simply have to gun down bucks while sparing does that populate three stages. The only real twist is that your money ticks down along with the timer, so you need to kill deer rapidly to keep playing. That mechanic is reused for a much better game that you’ll see higher on this list, so Bang For Your Buck doesn’t have much going for it beyond the obvious hunting satire. But as a piece of worldbuilding? It’s pure Florida, and I’m glad that it exists in Leonida.

Street Trash 3: Dezombifier is GTA 6’s very own Vampire Survivors clone. It’s a top-down twin-stick shooter where the goal is to gun through dense waves of zombies (and skeletons, for some reason) as you hunt for gears. As a send-up, it’s a little hit-and-miss. The roguelite is fun enough with its reliable choose-three level-up system, though it could have benefited from adopting Vampire Survivors’ more intuitive auto-firing action. It’s a little less effective as satire than some other entries on his list, since it feels more like a parody of AAA action games, complete with its quippy narrator. Still, it’s a fun little distraction that even has its own unlock system to keep you playing and find new weapons.

Arguably the funniest and most unexpected gag in all of GTA 6, Tenebrae Lux is Rockstar at the height of its satirical powers. The black-and-white puzzle game is a send-up of arthouse indie games created by auteur developers. More specifically, it’s a parody of Jonathan Blow, the creator of The Witness and Order of the Sinking Star. The convoluted experience (created solely by fictional developer Johannes Zuch) sees you exploring a mysterious island as a pompous narrator waxes poetic about philosophy. Funny enough, it’s a pretty well-designed puzzle game with galaxy-brained solutions. While it’s debatably a little too cerebral to enjoy casually, it’s an undeniably great spoof that respects this kind of game enough to lampoon them so perfectly.

The better of GTA 6’s two twin-stick shooters, Time Jackers Rewind is an over-the-top sci-fi game. A wisecracking soldier’s attempt to take down DominiCorp hits a snag when he accidentally travels through time. He gets some time powers in the process, but the twist is that he will die if he runs out of juice. You can only top it off by killing mutants, which basically makes Time Jackers Rewind a Crank video game in my book. It's a fast-paced shooter that pushes you to perfect your route through the city as you strategically acquire enough power to stay alive. It’s just a great mechanical premise, even if you take away the loudmouthed hero who is constantly tossing out hilariously hammy one-liners.

#3415. From a gown purchased with wartime rations to a secret engraving on the ring: Inside the historic royal wedding of Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip

Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip married in 1947, going on to make history by achieving the longest marriage of any British sovereign couple. Back then they were, of course, Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark, tying the knot in the rather austere years of post-war Britain. So, what really happened on their wedding day?

November 2, 1947: Queen Elizabeth—then Princess Elizabeth—with Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (right) and members of the immediate and extended Royal Family at Buckingham Palace after their wedding

The Queen and Prince Philip’s love story began back in 1939. Princess Elizabeth was just 13 years old; her dashing distant cousin, Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark, was five years her senior and about to join the Royal Navy. They met as she toured the Royal Naval College at Dartmouth; he was the young officer assigned to escort her around that day.

Determined to marry for love, Elizabeth was said to be rather taken with Philip, who was described at the time as ‘handsome as any film star.’ The pair were soon writing letters to each other, and later, occasional chaperoned meetings took place.

In 1946 Philip proposed in Scotland, and she immediately said yes. However, her father, King George, reportedly insisted the couple resist announcing their engagement until the Princess, who was just 20, was a little older. In the end, her parents gave in to her wishes, and Philip officially proposed to Princess Elizabeth in 1947, with a three-carat diamond ring he designed using stones taken from a family tiara that belonged to his mother, Princess Alice of Battenberg. It was created by London jeweller Philip Antrobus Ltd.

Princess Elizabeth with Philip Mountbatten on their wedding day

The Royal Family were adamant that the wedding of Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip would reflect the country’s post-war situation while also offering a chance for the nation to celebrate.

Like many brides at the time, Princess Elizabeth had to save her rationing coupons to buy the materials for her dress but was given an extra 200 from the government to help. While well-wishers generously sent their own to the royal, they had to be sent back as rules dictated that coupons could not be shared outside of households.

Designed by Norman Hartnell, Princess Elizabeth’s wedding dress was made from ivory silk, duchesse satin and silver thread; the dress featured crystals, 10,000 seed pearls, a fitted bodice, heart-shaped neckline, long sleeves and a 15-foot train. It was made in just seven weeks by 350 skilled women since the wedding took place only four months after the couple’s engagement announcement. Norman Hartnell also designed Elizabeth’s going-away outfit.

Princess Elizabeth’s wedding day tiara was called the Queen Mary Fringe Tiara. It had belonged to her grandmother, Queen Mary, and had been given to her as a wedding present in 1893. It was remade from a tiara/necklace that Queen Victoria had bought from Collingwood and Co.

As Elizabeth was getting ready on the morning of the wedding, it snapped. Luckily, royal jeweler Garrard was apparently on hand to fix it, and the Queen later revealed, “I think he taped up the spring.”

Princess Elizabeth’s other wedding day jewelry included two pearl necklaces. The shorter of the two necklaces was the “Queen Anne” necklace, said to have belonged to Anne, the last Stuart Queen. The other was known as the “Queen Caroline,” and is said to have belonged to the wife of King George II. Both necklaces were left to the Crown by Queen Victoria and were given to Elizabeth as a wedding present by her father.

All royal bridal bouquets contain myrtle from a myrtle bush planted by Queen Victoria at Osborne House. Princess Elizabeth’s also had white orchids and was laid on the grave of the Unknown Warrior at Westminster Abbey the day after the wedding.

There were eight bridesmaids at Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip’s wedding: Princess Margaret, Princess Alexandra, Lady Pamela Mountbatten, Diana Bowes-Lyon, Lady Elizabeth Lambart, Margaret Elphinstone, Lady Caroline Montagu-Douglas-Scott, and Lady Mary Cambridge.

Her two pages were Prince William of Gloucester and Prince Michael of Kent, both aged five at the time.

The bridesmaids were given silver Art Deco-style compacts with the couple's initials and a crown engraved on the lid, set with five cabochon sapphires.

The Duke of Edinburgh's best man was David Mountbatten, the Marquess of Milford Haven.

Knowing that Elizabeth hated cigarettes, Prince Philip reportedly gave up smoking on the morning of his wedding “suddenly and apparently without difficulty,” according to his valet, John Dean.

The wedding took place at Westminster Abbey on November, 20th, 1947 at 11:30 a.m. Princess Elizabeth was the 10th member of the Royal Family to be married at Westminster Abbey.

Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip walking down the aisle of Westminster Abbey, followed by their bridesmaids and pages

There were 2,000 guests in attendance, including the likes of the King of Iraq, Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard of the Netherlands and the Hereditary Grand Duke of Luxembourg and Princess Elisabeth of Luxembourg. The ceremony was broadcast on the radio to millions of listeners.

Together with her father, Princess Elizabeth left Buckingham Palace in the Irish State Coach. (In her later years, it had been Queen Victoria’s state carriage of choice, as she declined to use the Gold State Coach following the death of Prince Albert.)

The wedding ceremony was officiated by the Archbishop of Canterbury, Geoffrey Fisher, and the Archbishop of York, Cyril Garbett.

The organist and Master of the Choristers at the Abbey, Australian William Neil McKie, was the director of music for the wedding and there were 91 singers; the abbey choir was joined by the choirs of the Chapel Royal and St George's Chapel in Windsor.

The service started with a specially composed fanfare by Arnold Bax and finished with Felix Mendelssohn's “Wedding March,” with ceremony hymns including “Praise, my Soul, the King of Heaven” and “The Lord's my Shepherd.”

The bride and groom knelt on orange boxes covered in pink silk at the altar as a nod to post-war austerity.

On the day of the wedding, Philip was given the title of Duke of Edinburgh by his father-in-law, King George VI. After the Queen ascended the throne in 1953, she made the decision in 1957 to make Philip a prince of the UK, in addition to his dukedom.

The wedding rings were made from a nugget of Welsh gold which came from the Clogau St David's mine, near Dolgellau.

According to Royal biographer Ingrid Seward, who wrote Prince Philip: Revealed, Philip had a secret message inscribed inside his wife's wedding band, a message that only the engraver, Queen Elizabeth, and her husband knew the contents of.

After the service, a wedding breakfast was held in the Ball-Supper Room at Buckingham Palace for 150 guests only, with Filet de Sole Mountbatten, Perdreau en Casserole and Bombe Glacée Princess Elizabeth on the menu.

During the breakfast, the string band of the Grenadier Guards played music while guests were greeted with individual posies of myrtle and white Balmoral on their place settings as the wedding favors.

The couple waving from the balcony of Buckingham Palace

Famously, the newlyweds went onto the balcony at Buckingham Palace to wave to the huge crowds on the Mall.

Although the royal couple received 11 wedding cakes, the official traditional fruit cake was baked by McVitie and Price and was four tiers and nine feet high. The wedding cake was decorated with both coats of arms, including the monograms of the bride and groom, sugar-iced figures of their favorite activities, and regimental and naval badges.

Mr Schur, chief confectioner at McVitie and Price, putting the final touches to the wedding cake

The newlyweds cut the cake using the Duke's Mountbatten sword, which was a wedding present from the King.

Over 10,000 people sent telegrams congratulating Elizabeth and Philip, and around 2,500 wedding presents were sent from around the world. These included a cloth from Mahatma Gandhi that he’d woven himself, which Queen Mary mistook for an “indelicate” loincloth.

After their wedding breakfast, Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip headed to Waterloo station, joined by Elizabeth’s corgi, Susan, catching a train to Hampshire to spend their wedding night in Broadlands, the home of Philip's uncle, Earl Mountbatten.

The rest of their royal honeymoon was spent at Birkhall on the Balmoral Estate in Scotland.

Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip being showered with rose petals as they leave Buckingham Palace, London, for their honeymoon.

#3414. Focker In-Law Review: Ben Stiller And Ariana Grande Bring New Laughs To An Old Franchise

There's an unwritten rule that says most comedy film franchises suffer from diminishing returns. In general, it's hard to dispute that claim, as even several solid examples of funny comedy sequels tend to lack the freshness and originality of their predecessors. Thanks to this phenomenon, the existence of good comedy sequels, and especially good comedy franchises, feels almost unheard of.

That said, the "Meet the Parents" franchise is one that has quietly yet persistently endured over the past 26 years. (Even longer than that, if you consider the fact that the 2000 film is in fact a remake of the hard-to-find 1992 original.) The initial film in the series, starring Ben Stiller as the hapless, unfortunately named Greg Focker, debuted early during the '00s "cringe comedy" trend, part of a wave of films and shows which delighted in the awkwardly relatable suffering of its protagonists. The family sitcom nature of the film helped lead to two more sequels, "Meet the Fockers" and "Little Fockers." The latter movie appeared to close out what was a trilogy for the last 16 years, until the release of "Focker In-Law" this month.

Given Hollywood's recent over-reliance on pre-existing IP, it wouldn't have been surprising to see such a movie be a lazy legacy sequel, milking the franchise for anything it had left (despite its lack of nipples). This is why the film is such a pleasant surprise, as it manages to recapture much of what made "Meet the Parents" hilarious without resorting to too many callback bits. Rather than merely flipping the first film's script and having the legacy cast pass the torch to younger characters, "Focker In-Law" impressively continues Greg's journey. Its a film whose cast and crew manage to find new laughs within an old franchise.

Being a legacy sequel, "Focker In-Law" naturally brings back as many of the characters seen throughout the prior movies as it can. In addition to Ben Stiller's Greg, his wife Pam (Teri Polo), her father Jack (Robert De Niro), his wife Dina (Blythe Danner), and even Pam's ex-fiancé Kevin (Owen Wilson) appear here. (Those hoping to see Greg's parents Bernie and Roz, played in the past by Barbara Streisand and Dustin Hoffman, are out of luck.)

Thanks to the 16 year gap between sequels, Greg and Pam's children Henry and Samantha have grown up, and are now played by Skyler Gisondo and Beanie Feldstein, respectively. The plot is "Meet the Parents" in reverse; where that film saw Greg attempt to ingratiate himself with Jack before marrying Pam, now Henry is bringing home a woman he's hoping to marry: Olivia Jones (Ariana Grande).

It would've been easy for writer/director John Hamburg (who devised the story along with Ilana Glazer and Austen Earl) to pull a "The Force Awakens" on "Meet the Parents" and follow either Henry as he attempts to convince his dad and grandfather about his fiancé, or Olivia as she tries to win them over herself. Instead, Hamburg smartly keeps the focus on Greg's empty nest anxieties, allowing the franchise to grow older with him rather than try to pivot to a younger generation. It's a savvy choice, particularly because it doesn't require anyone to fill Stiller's shoes. After all, Stiller has not only perfected this character but also the comedic tone of the films. "Focker In-Law" contains some gags that would easily be over the top in the hands of someone less experienced, but Stiller can make Greg foolish while being sympathetic enough so things never go too far.

There's no getting around the fact that "Focker In-Law" is a mainstream studio comedy sequel, and as such it does occasionally fall prey to some of the pitfalls of that genre. For one thing, it's not a particularly striking looking film. While that's on par with the rest of the franchise (which never seemed too interested in focusing on production design or cinematography), it's a shame that it mostly relies on a standardized aesthetic to be broadly appealing rather than going for something unique. The scourge of broadness does also crop up in some of the gags, including the moment where a series of mishaps causes Jack to be "baby birded" someone else's food at the dinner table, which is easily the most groan-worthy joke in the film.

That said, it's commendable that such a joke is the summit of the film's lowest common denominator, for the bulk of the set pieces are expertly constructed. A running joke about Jack's aggressive dog hating Greg escalates to a degree of chaos that's worthy of vintage John Hughes, something that's not easy to do given that writer's hugely influential status. In the same way John Hamburg could've given into temptation to make "Focker In-Law" a more conventional legacy sequel, he also could've fallen into the trap of making this sequel bigger and crazier.

Instead, his history with the franchise means he innately understands that the films' bread and butter lies in steady escalation rather than sharp left turns. Ben Stiller can be set on fire and then almost frozen alive later, but such stunts wouldn't work if they weren't deployed correctly. Hamburg and company know just how much and what type of track to lay for the train to reach the station.

The secret sauce of "Focker In-Law" is that it succeeds thanks to a thorough commitment to character. All the best comedy is character-based. While Ben Stiller's Greg is the film's centerpoint, the supporting characters are just as vital. Robert De Niro gives Jack a warmer demeanor this time around. Owen Wilson turns up Kevin's smarm to 11. Skyler Gisondo proves once again how deft a performer he can be, making Henry a comedic variant on his Decoy Dan from "Primetime," as he tries to be his own person while attempting to placate a father figure.

Ariana Grande has perhaps the hardest task in the movie, as her Olivia needs to walk the line between sweet girl next door and, in Greg's eyes, a master manipulator villainess. Her excellent performance allows the film to indulge in some broad tonal swings while keeping Olivia believable as a human rather than a caricature.

For folks whom "Meet the Parents" and its sequels were more excruciating experiences than hilarious comedies, "Focker In-Law" isn't going to change your mind. Yet for those of us who've related to Greg Focker's plight and foolish behavior over the years, the film is a little gift. It still has a broad relatability in its observations on family and relationships. Yet it's also refreshing in how it commits to following Greg on his never-ending journey to be a better person. Thanks to this commitment, "Focker In-Law" has given its franchise a new lease on laughs.

"Focker In-Law" is in theaters on November 25, 2026.

Disneyland live entertainment is few and far between as of late, which is a shame considering the Anaheim theme park used to boast some of the best shows. On November 21st, one of the last and most beloved nighttime shows, Fantasmic, went up in flames for the second time in three short years. With two incidents and Disney’s desire to cut back on live entertainment, I’m really starting to worry about the future of the show.

The fire reportedly broke out during Fantasmic’s second performance of the night shortly before the show’s finale. While the Mark Twain finale was able to go on, flames can be seen behind the boat on the small stage set up on Tom Saywer Island. Guests at the park were quick to pull out their phones and film the growing flames as the Mark Twain, full of classic Disney characters, made its way around the river. Take a look:

Here’s the Mark Twain Riverboat running during Fantasmic last night with the fire behind it. This happened during the 10:30PM show https://t.co/bMcOZ6z0PtNovember 22, 2026

The last two minutes of the show were canceled, and guests were asked to vacate the viewing area while the fire department handled the blaze. Thankfully, the fire was small compared to the 2023 incident that turned the Maleficent dragon animatronic into a giant fireball and forever changed the show. There’s been no word on the extent of the damage this time around, but considering the show was back Sunday night it safe to assume that nothing was affected and no cast members were harmed, thankfully.

Two fiery incidents are definitely a cause for concern, and with Disneyland executives’ history of scaling back entertainment to cut costs, I can’t help but worry about the show’s fate. After all, Fantasmic boasts a large cast of incredible performers and several floating units. Plus water screens, projectors, and fireworks. I’m no expert, but I’m willing to bet it’s one of the most costly attractions at Disneyland. Not to mention, the show is still feeling the loss of the Maleficent Dragon, which makes the battle between Mickey and Maleficent lackluster.

While I don’t think Disneyland would end the show without also announcing a replacement, I do think Disney fans should prepare themselves. After all, Disney fans aren’t known for taking new changes well. Just look at the uproar that happened when it was announced Dinosaur would close to make room for a new Indiana Jones attraction at Disney World.

Disneyland has been having a rough go at things this month. On the first day of the holiday season, the Anaheim theme park’s iconic fake snow was accidentally turned on during a rainstorm, creating a mess. Back in October, Frontierland experienced widespread flooding. With park tickets being so expensive, it’s unfortunate to see cracks in Disneyland’s magic, but not even the mouse can control the weather or unexpected fires.

#3411. Who Will Be The Next Bond Girl?

Since the beginning of the week, the James Bond frenzy has shown no signs of stopping. On November 16, new Bond owners Amazon MGM Studios finally revealed the name of the actor who will succeed Daniel Craig as 007: Robert Pattinson. After years of speculation and months of intense rumors, the next James Bond now has a new face. Now, the next question on everyone’s mind: Who will be the next Bond girl?

The exception in thie great debate is Léa Seydoux. The actor, who seems to be everywhere this year, played Madeleine Swann in Craig's final Bond films, Spectre (2015) and No Time to Die (2021). Her magnetic performance made Madeleine an unforgettable Bond girl, especially since her character plays a decisive role in the arc of Craig’s character: at the end of No Time to Die, the famous spy sacrifices himself to save her and their daughter, Mathilde. For the first time since its creation in 1953 by British author Ian Fleming, the secret agent in Her Majesty’s service was gone.

Léa Seydoux and Daniel Craig pose as they arrive on the set of No Time To Die on September 09, 2019 in Matera, Italy.

In a recent interview on Vogue's The Run-Through podcast, Seydoux was candid about how little interest she had in her successor. “I don’t really care,” she said with a laugh. “I don’t really care, guys. How can you?”

When pressed on who Pattinson's female lead might be, Seydoux expressed mixed feelings about the British spy's latest iteration. With the purchase of the Bond IP by Amazon, “It became American," Seydoux said. “But I’m sure the movie will be great because it’s directed by Denis Villeneuve, who’s a very talented director. I’m sure he will do something great.”

The online megamart took control of the storied franchise in 2023, after which Amazon founder Jeff Bezos controversially sought feedback on the title character's casting via X. The announcement of Villeneuve as the next film's director brought things back from the brink.

Bezos, who confirmed that he was “very involved” in the film's casting process, also seems to give Seydoux pause. In an interview with Variety, she admitted “was a bit sad when I heard that it was sold (…) but now that it’s Denis, I was like, Oh, at least it’s him, so it will be cinema.”

Denis Villeneuve, who directed Seydoux in Dune: Part Two, will release the final installment of this epic science-fiction trilogy will be on December 16. After that, he'll be free to focus on his next major project: reviving the world’s most famous secret agent. It remains to be seen who he will choose to star opposite Robert Pattinson as his female companion—but we know that despite her fondness for the director, Seydoux will not return: Just last month, the French actress told People “I really loved being on this franchise, but now it’s ... done.”

#3410. Prime Video's God Of War Series Is Bringing One Video Game Cast Member Into Live-Action

The upcoming "God of War" TV series is bringing back a very recognizable face from the smash-hit games that inspired it. In the latest significant bit of casting for the Prime Video adaptation, actor Deborah Ann Woll has been chosen to reprise her voice role as Faye (aka Laufey), the late wife of Kratos, who looms incredibly large throughout the events of both mainline games and the upcoming spin-off titled "God of War Laufey." The news comes straight from Sony Pictures Television and Amazon MGM Studios, with the official press release describing the character as:

"The mysterious late wife of Kratos and mother of Atreus, Faye's abrupt passing sets in motion the events of 'God of War.' Along their journey, Kratos and Atreus discover secrets about Faye that make them wonder how well they truly knew her at all."

As gamers know, Faye's death prior to the events of the 2018 "God of War" game — the first in the more modern-generation games that shifted the action to Norse mythology — essentially kicked off the journey of Kratos and his young son Atreus as they discover hidden threats, newfound allies, and a much wider world than either character ever could've imagined. The "Daredevil" star now joins a packed cast that includes Dave Bautista as Kratos (taking over for original star Ryan Hurst, who injured himself during filming), Callum Vinson as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin, Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor, Alastair Duncan as Mimir, and plenty more.

Look, if you can't beat your pitch-perfect casting from the first time around, then you might as well bring them back again. Deborah Ann Woll lent her voice and facial model to the character of Faye, starting with the 2018 "God of War" game, continuing with the highly-acclaimed sequel "Ragnarök," and soon taking on the lead role (yes, despite the inconvenience of Faye's death) in 2027's "God of War Laufey." Now, she's set to suit up in live-action for the Prime Video series, which is set to run for two full seasons as our next major video game adaptation.

This is both a strong vote of confidence in Woll's abilities as a performer (who most recently reprised her role as Karen Page in "Daredevil: Born Again") and an acknowledgement that, for certain characters, the original voice actor was simply the perfect choice all along. It's incredibly easy to imagine her bringing the same amount of pathos, tragedy, and bittersweet moments amid various flashbacks and visions that Kratos experiences throughout the saga ... and, perhaps, even in some original scenes further fleshing out their strong dynamic in the show. After all, when you have someone as talented and capable as Woll to work with, you might as well make full use of her time.

Prime Video's "God of War" series comes from showrunner Ronald D. Moore, with "Shōgun" and "Fallout" director Frederick E.O. Toye helming the first two episodes of Season 1. After a brief pause following Ryan Hurst's injury and the subsequent recasting of Dave Bautista, the show is currently on track for a likely 2027 release. Stay tuned to /Film for more casting and production updates as they come in.

#3409. Goodbye, Mandy: GTA 6 Players Are Already Obsessed With Someone Else

As Grand Theft Auto 6 began releasing around the world last week, players quickly became obsessed with Mandy. She's a neighbor of Jason's who tries to seduce the himbo while he fixes her sink. (And she is totally not a serial killer, no way, why would you ask?) Mandy shows up early in GTA 6. But as more players advance in the game, they're becoming obsessed with a new character: Vicki, a standout character from Chapter 2.

[Ed. note: Light spoilers for the end of Chapter 1 and beginning of Chapter 2 follow. We'll keep them vague.]

After Jason is injured at the end of Chapter 1, Lucia takes him to a run-down motel to lie low. She wants to find stronger painkillers for him, which leads her to Vicki. She's a goth exotic dancer who also moonlights as a small-time drug dealer, and immediately pulls one over on Lucia by selling her over-the-counter Zombix (GTA's brand of painkiller) for $50. Lucia then barges back into Vicki's room and demands the drugs she paid for, which takes the two on a trip around Port Gellhorn. They get Vicki's paycheck from Delights Cabaret and save her friend Dunk from a gang, all the while getting to know one another. They bond over the fact that they're both moms trying to support their kids by whatever means necessary.

Players have quickly fallen for Vicki. "Love her she's my favorite character so far," one player wrote on Reddit.

"Punk Ana de Armas," another said, and, you know, I can kinda see it.

Vicki is voiced by Taryn Manning, who's best known for her role in Orange Is the New Black. She's also starred in 8 Mile, Hustle and Flow, and Hawaii Five-0.

Manning's work as Vicki is part of the reason why players are flocking to her. "Mandy didn't do it for me, but Vicki did because I recognized Taryn Manning’s voice immediately," one Redditor said.

"Vicki the baddie that made everyone move on from Mandy lmao," another said.

Basically, you can tell how far thirsty GTA 6 players are getting in the game based on who they're obsessively posting about over on the Grand Theft Auto subreddits. In a few days, as players continue to marathon Rockstar's hit, I'm sure they'll have a new favorite.

For six seasons now, Abbott Elementary fans have faithfully watched the relationship between Janine Teagues (Quinta Brunson) and Gregory Eddie (Tyler James Williams) progress. The pair have gone from good friends to committed lovers over the past several years and, now, it seems we’re on the cusp of a proposal. Many viewers are hoping an engagement will come during the Disneyland-set 100th episode that’ll air amid the 2026 TV schedule. I’d love that as well, but I also have a question about two other characters.

Gregory and Janine are, of course, the core couple on Abbott, but plenty of other romantic relationships amongst characters have been highlighted as well. As we anticipate what lies ahead for Janine and Gregory, I can’t help but wonder what the future holds for Ava Coleman and O’Shon, who’ve been dating since Season 4. I’ve enjoyed seeing their relationship develop as well as the funny moments that have resulted from that. With that, it’s hard not to wonder what the long-term plan for them might look like.

It’s clear that the affable O’Shon (Matthew Law) and Abbott’s diva of a principal Ava (Critics Choice winner Janelle James) are on steady footing after some initial growing pains. At this point, the pair have not only vacationed together, but they’ve also reached the point where they can throw a party as a couple. (That Halloween shindig they held this season was fantastic). Some may think it’s a bit early to consider a proposal for these two, but I don’t think it’s wild to think it could happen by the end of Season 6.

Gregory first expressed interest in proposing to Janine at the end of Season 5, which was about two years after the two finally got together. Ava and O’Shon will be reaching that mark later in the sixth season and, while great TV couples have different timelines, I could see O’Shon popping the question soon. Plus, given how encouraging O’Shon has been amid Gregory’s attempts to propose, who’s to say the former doesn’t want that for himself sometime in the near future?

Of course, I’m not saying anyone needs to be jumping the broom by the end of this season. I just wouldn’t mind seeing one or two engagements by the time Abbott’s finale rolls around next spring. That may seem like a long shot for Ava and O’Shon right now, but I’m feeling very good about Janine and Gregory’s chances of hitting that milestone.

The True Story That Inspired Abbott Elementary’s Choice To Move The School Into A Mall

Gregory has been trying to orchestrate the right moment to present Janine with a ring. During the show’s latest episode, “Competition,” he attempted to land a reservation at a popular Italian restaurant, where he could propose. Ironically, that plan became moot once Abbott’s Step Team punched their ticket to Disneyland, and Janine informed her man that they’d serve as chaperones on the trip. So it now seems like a given that Gregory will attempt to propose while he and his lady are in “The Happiest Place On Earth.”

What’s more is that the pressure is going to be on, as Janine is aware of her beau’s intention to pop the question (thanks to a major slip-up on Ava’s part). So the pressure is really on for Eddie to craft the perfect proposal. The Disneyland episode could indeed present him the right situation to do just that and, if Gregory does pull it off in great fashion, it might set a bit of a bar for O’Shon to clear if he eventually takes that step.

We’ll just have to wait and see how it plays out when Abbott Elementary airs its hundredth episode on Wednesday, December 2 at 8:30 p.m. ET on ABC. Fans can also stream the show the next day with a Hulu subscription.

For adventurers and outdoor enthusiasts who want more than the average smartwatch, Garmin sets the standard with its industry-leading features and durability. Fortunately, with Amazon’s early Black Friday sale, you can get one of its bestsellers, the 44mm Garmin Instinct 3 AMOLED, for 44% off at $249.99 (originally $449.99).

The 1.2-inch color AMOLED display makes the screen more readable in bright daylight conditions, and battery life is best-in-class, lasting up to 18 days (even longer when you’re not using it regularly), which reduces the need for weekly charging, a must for those going off-grid. Durability is also a major perk, with features like a metal-reinforced bezel, chemically strengthened glass, and a 10 ATM water rating, which makes it suitable for underwater activities.

It comes with a built-in flashlight and multi-band GPS, supported by Garmin’s SatIQ technology to better balance location accuracy and battery use, while tracking features include heart rate, sleep, blood oxygen, and other wellness metrics. There’s no shortage of training tools for workouts and outdoor activities, and like regular smartwatches, it displays alerts like texts and emails when paired with an iPhone or Android. The Garmin Pay feature is another bonus for those who don’t want to have their wallet on them at all times.

If you want to log your activities, whether that’s skiing the slopes, heading out on a long trail run, or going on a camping trip in the woods, the 44mm Garmin Instinct 3 AMOLED is a rugged option with plenty of useful tools for those who love the outdoors. And you can’t forget its wildly impressive battery life. At $200 off, it’s a powerful entry into the Garmin world that can accomplish a lot and won’t set you back nearly as much as the brand’s more loaded watches.

#3406. The Method-Dressing Madness Behind Mckenna Grace‘s 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' Press Tour Looks

Before the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping press tour began, Mckenna Grace knew she wanted to be method dressed for her appearances. Made a household term by Law Roach and Zendaya, method dressing is when actors wear looks that pay homage to the film or show they’re promoting: See Zendaya’s on-theme looks across red carpets for Dune, Spiderman, and The Odyssey for a slew of examples.

With the new Hunger Games film, it’s Grace’s turn to adopt the trend. A super fan of the Suzanne Collins book series and their film adaptations, Grace—who plays District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner—took a hand in the styling for her press run, weaving easter eggs into every look. Her stylist, Molly Dickson, was up for the challenge of translating Grace’s deep-cut references into custom and archival looks from Monique Lhuillier, Gucci, Celine and more.

In a wide-ranging conversation, Dickson breaks down all the looks that set the Hunger Games fans’ hearts aflame, from Rue’s blue dress to Katniss’ Mockingjay gown, and all the threads that came together for Grace’s most memorable press appearances yet.

Vanity Fair: How did you get into styling?

Molly Dickson: I went to college in Minnesota and my major was advertising. Two weeks before I graduated, I called my mom and said, "I'm not into this. I don't wanna do advertising." She said, "Well, what do you wanna do?" I told her, "I wanna do fashion. I wanna go to New York." She said, "No, absolutely not."

Right after I graduated, I went to LA, this was 2009 during the recession, and no one was hiring. I got an internship at Marie Claire in New York, and enrolled back into college to get school credit to intern at Hearst. I worked at Marie Claire as a market assistant for almost two years, and then I left and assisted Leslie Fremar for seven years. That's when I fell in love with celebrity. Then ten years ago, I went off on my own.

What would you say are your aesthetic influences as a stylist?

My personal style relates very similarly to Sadie Sink's style, very effortless. She always wants to be very comfortable and easy, never anything frilly or over the top. Just a simple, beautiful dress, and you let it speak for itself.

Mckenna is a big fan of the original film series, so it’s clear you’re pulling from there as influences when dressing her. Is it a collaborative process when coming to one of these referential looks?

She's obviously a very huge fan of the franchise. We actually started having conversations about this tour in April, which is very early to start having conversations. I could just sense her excitement around it. She started sending me mood boards, and I actually looked back today at the mood board and it was, it was a lot of Katniss Everdeen. It had Joanna on it, and it was filled with these really strong female characters from the franchise.

What she really wanted to hit was Katniss’ wedding gown look and the Mockingjay look with the wings. I was really stumped on how to pull that off without making it overly costumey.

Mckenna kept asking, "What's going on with those?" I knew the vision, but I didn't know how to execute it. I was working with Keke Palmer and the designer Michael Ngo. He was making some cool music costumes for Keke, and I asked, "Michael, could you make this silver piece?" 'Cause I really had no idea how to get it done.

He said, “I don't think I can do that. You know what? Just give me a day, let me play around with it." That night, he said, "I figured it out." We got the piece and I thought, "Okay, it needs to be a wedding dress under,” so I reached out to all the bridal houses. I wanted it to be vintage because it would tell a pretty story. Monique [Lhuillier] ended up sending a ton of wedding gowns, and the day before Mckenna came in for the fitting, I actually tried the wedding dresses on myself with the silver piece.

I sent Mckenna five dresses, and the one that she ended up wearing, she said, "That's it. I don't even need to try anything else. That's the one I'm gonna wear." Then, it was a matter of finding the right event to wear it to because it’s pretty nice, very dramatic.

She was in Paris for the Miu Miu show, and I brought it there because she had the Hunger Games Museum event. It was a whole conversation with her team, like, "Is it the right moment? Is it too much for this event?" Her PR said, "No, this is the perfect moment. It's the best way to kick off the tour." The response with the Hunger Games fans—I have never seen anything like it before, ever.

What was the experience of having her be such a big part of the styling process?

It makes my job so fun because she is so passionate about it and she loves Hunger Games so much, even just finding subtle nods back to the movie. She would say, "I wanna do a ladybug look." Thom Browne did that amazing ladybug dress, I thought, "That's so cool, but it's not really her personal aesthetic." So it’s finding ways to keep it still true to her personal style while maintaining the nods to the film.

The way you seem to understand Mckenna feels something similar to the connection between Katniss and Cinna in The Hunger Games. When pulling looks for her, what comes into play? How do you make her come through and not be lost in the lore of the stories or the dress?

Mckenna had said that she maybe wanted to do a red or a dark pink feather look because in the books [Maysilee] gets attacked by the red birds which are like flamingos. I'm pulling in all these red feather dresses and on the runway, this one dress looked amazing. Mckenna said, “That's perfect for the flamingo reference.”

But we put it on her and it was so big, and she's so petite so she was just getting swarmed. I said, “Let"s not force it.” The goal was for her to feel comfortable in the look rather than just getting each reference.

The public has been really excited about these looks. Are you thinking about the response to the looks when you’re putting them together?

There's been some conversations in a fitting, like, "Oh, the Hunger Games fans are gonna get this." They're gonna see the inspiration, they're gonna understand it.

But I wouldn't say we're choosing a look because ‘Oh, this is gonna go viral to the Hunger Games community.’ Mckenna is a super fan herself so if she's getting excited about the look, everyone else that's a fan of the franchise is gonna get excited about the look.

Do you feel any pressure to top the last outfit after each premiere?

Yes. I think it was Paris because that wedding dress did get so much press. In that fitting, it felt like, "We gotta keep our game up high." It's been really fun for my team and market assistants because a lot of the girls that work with me are huge fans of the movie. They're not even seeing it as work. They're like, "Oh my God, this is so exciting. Look at this. This looks like this from the movie."

What was the inspiration to do method dressing for this press run? What do you think is the value?

Mckenna knew back in April, she said, "I wanna do method for this." I personally did not read the books. I'm a visual person, so I've seen all the movies. Lionsgate was able to let me go with the cast when they first saw the movie because my agent was like, "Molly needs to go to the movie to get inspired before this press tour. She can't do a method dressing press tour without seeing the movie."

Even as the tour was going on, Mckenna kept sending me new references and quotes from the book and stuff like that.

What made you take it to the next level? From paying homage to not only characters, but the actual actors from the films like Jennifer Lawrence at the 2011 Oscars to even dressing like set pieces from the film.

That was all Mckenna's vision. On her first mood board, she had a lot of Jennifer Lawrence's red carpet moments because she's such a huge fan of Katniss and Jennifer Lawrence.

With the Rue reference, Mckenna thought that color was just very Hunger Games. It wasn't until she put the dress on, her mom said, "Wait, this is Rue's dress." So that was just fate. I would love to take credit for that.

Why do you think that this styling has generated so much attention?

I think it’s when you do method dressing for such a big franchise and you really are passionate about it. The thing is that Mckenna is so excited and passionate about this movie. She has said, “I didn't think that I would love doing fittings so much. I used to hate doing fittings.”

Because every look is so intentionally tied back to Hunger Games and she's such a big fan, it's literally like playing dress up with her. I think the fans see it, she's so relatable because she's a fan that all these fans think, "Wow, like, she's a fan and she got to do this." She’s the fangirl living out her dream, and the fans are excited for her that she finally gets to do this.

What do you think are the best kinds of projects to implement method dressing with/works best with? What does it work best with?

I think the big movies that already have a fan base, like Barbie or Wednesday, Being able to pull inspiration from existing books or films makes it so much easier for a stylist rather than a movie that no one's seen before. There's no curiosity or momentum about it because you're starting from scratch, whereas Hunger Games, Barbie, Wednesday, there's already a level of expectation.

The looks for this press run have been a mix of archival, new, and custom pieces. How do you make that choice? How important is it for you to create an archive for Mckenna?

It kind of is a mix of what we’re able to source. Mckenna really wanted to pay homage to Joanna's character with that scene where she's like, "My stylist is always putting me in trees." She's like, "I wanna do a tree reference." And I'm like, "How in the world am I gonna find a fashion reference that's a tree that's not a costume?"

I love the challenge of sourcing the market, and so do the girls on my team. I think it was 2011 Phoebe Philo where Celine did some tree references in the collection. But just because we find it online doesn't mean that we can get it. So then it's reaching out to every vintage dealer, every rental house, asking, "Do you guys have anything like this?" And they might have it, but they're like, "It's already gone, someone has it." I ended up actually finding the Celine tree dress on the RealReal, and I bought it. I love RealReal.

What is your approach to dressing different clients? For instance, you mentioned Sadie Sink earlier, can you walk me through how that process differs from Mckenna?

It's very different between each girl. I let them set the pace. If they wanna be involved, great. If they just wanna show up to the fitting and not even know what's gonna be there, I try to accommodate whatever direction they wanna go. I have one client that literally last week has sent me over 200 references of dresses that she wants, and another girl that's like, “I really don't care. Whatever you tell me to wear, I'll wear it.”

Every girl is different, and what makes my job so interesting is that it's not the same. Everyone has very different styles. I think the most important part of a job as a stylist is to keep their style true to them and not just force my style onto them. Mckenna's way more girly, Sadie is a little bit more casual, it’s just taking their style and elevating it a little bit.

Will you do any looks inspired by Mckenna’s character Maysilee? The looks have been mostly referential to things and people from past stories. Are there influences of Maysilee in the looks that fans haven't been able to pick up on because the film wasn’t out yet?

In a couple days, she’ll be in Miami for press, and she's wearing a very Maysilee inspired, purple Miu Miu dress that has a white collar. When she wears it, everyone's gonna be like, "Oh, that's Maysilee." She really wanted to have flowers and necklaces because Maysilee is really into jewelry, so it’s very light and flowery.

Can you break down the outfit for the New York City premiere?

We are doing the Mockingjay dress, the one with the wings, and that was another thing that I was very stumped on. I'm like, "What designer's gonna make these wings?" I had this woman in LA who does wings, she's done Halloween costumes and music videos.

In the first fitting, I pulled this navy Pamella Roland gown. The fabric is really, really cool. It's like a shimmery kind of organza. I thought, "That's the right color,” but I wanted it to be strapless. I went back to Pamella Roland and they were like, "We can make it in strapless." Mckenna was very keen on having some sort of embellishment to replicate Katniss because she had screen printing on the gown and it kind of looks like wings in a way.

Pamela then drew all these CADs with diamond wings on it, and then we got the wings made. We did the final fitting and I almost started to cry. Her mom's taking videos and it's epic. It's so exciting because the fans were doing polls on what she's gonna wear to the premiere.

It's full circle, we started with the wedding dress, Mckenna did the fire gown, and then we ended with the Mockingjay dress.

What was the hardest look to pull together?

I think design-wise, it was the fire gown.

Getting the fire printed on the fabric was really hard. I had a while back done a custom Cong Tri gown for Cami Mendes for the Masters of the Universe tour. It was like a gold beaded gown, and I remember I really liked the fabrics that they used for it.

So when I was thinking of who could do this fire gown, I reached out to them first, and I'm like, "Can you guys do something that looks like a fire? Like, she's literally on fire." And they're like, "No. We don't think we can." And again, they were like, "Give us some time." They came back and said, "We did all these testing on the fabric." I'm like, "Yeah, you did it. You did it."

What's really funny is we were at a fitting at Mckenna's house with the fire gown in a garment bag, and one of her friends stopped by. It was just a tip of the dress showing and her friend said, "Oh my God, you got a fire gown." Then I thought, "Okay, people are gonna get it."

#3404. One Element Of Avengers: Doomsday Has Me Excited Above All Else

"Avengers: Doomsday" is going to be one of the biggest movies of the year, if not ever, that much is certain. But so far, the movie's marketing has been quite, well, underwhelming. We already had one "Avengers" film (well, two) that relied entirely on gathering lots of known Marvel Cinematic Universe characters on screen at the same time. To do that again feels less special, as exciting as it is to see Cyclops (James Marsden) leading the X-Men into battle here.

Indeed, the worst thing one can say about this film right now is that it looks exactly like what you would expect. It's massive, sure, but it doesn't feel surprising in any way. Marvel announcing Robert Downey Jr. as Doctor Doom in the movie felt desperate, too, as it was obviously the studio's way of trying to win back the fans who'd been disappointed by the MCU's post-"Avengers: Endgame" output. "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" aside, Marvel's no longer the reliable hit machine that it once was.

That being said, there is one notable reason to be excited about "Doomsday." No, not the X-Men (though their inclusion is certainly cool) or the return of Scarlet Witch (Elizabeth Olsen). Instead, it's the fact that "Doomsday" is technically a direct sequel to "Thunderbolts*," itself by far the best non-"Spider-Man" MCU movie since "Endgame." More specifically, it picks up where that film left off, with the titular team (also known as the West Chesapeake Valley Thunderbolts sponsored by Shane's Tire Company) now officially being known as the New Avengers.

Sure enough, the final "Doomsday" trailer features a few shots of the New Avengers amidst all the new footage of Chris Evans as Steve Rogers, and it's enough to finally get me hyped for this film.

For the most part, the visuals in the final "Avengers: Doomsday" trailer look horrendously muted and dull, save for a single brief shot of David Harbour's Alexei Shostakov dressed in a horrendous New Avengers tracksuit staring in awe as Shang-Chi (Simu Liu) arrives at Avengers Tower. Immediately, the image both brightens the trailer and reminds you that as serious as "Doomsday" may be (with the old Avengers looking more tired and beaten up than ever), the New Avengers bring a whole different vibe to the table. After all, they're silly, not great at teamwork, and don't consider themselves to be gods. Instead, they talk through their psychological issues and even hug it out like something out of "Neon Genesis Evangelion."

As the final trailer makes clear, "Doomsday" is all about different superhero groups coming together. You have the remnants of the original Avengers team, the X-Men, the Thunderbolts/New Avengers, and the Fantastic Four — plus the stragglers from various MCU titles that we collectively kind of forgot about. Each brings a different dynamic to the film, with the New Avengers specifically being a group of loser superheroes and criminals not unlike the Guardians of the Galaxy ... with the big difference being that the former have to save themselves before they can save anyone else. It's why "Thunderbolts*" makes for such an emotional gut punch, especially when its leads come together as a team, and the idea of seeing them interact with the MCU at large does more to make "Doomsday" feel interesting than any number of cameos could.

"Avengers: Doomsday" will see the New Avengers suit up alongside their companions when it hits theaters on December 18, 2026.

Warning: There is discussion of suicide in this story.

It’s been seven months since Storage Wars star Darrell Sheets died by suicide in his home in Arizona, and it sounds like the other stars of the show, like Brandi Passante, are still, understandably, processing his death. Season 19 of the reality show kicks off on the 2026 television schedule on November 28th, and ahead of its premiere, Passante talked about Sheets’ passing and how it has affected both her personally and the production of the show.

Sheets left the show as a full-time cast member in 2019 after suffering a heart attack. He remained in contact with the rest of the cast, including Passante, and he made occasional guest appearances after retiring. In a discussion with TV Insider, Passante talked about how his death has affected the show, including how the rest of the cast work with each other:

It definitely changed the dynamic with everybody. We’re all a little softer and kinder to each other since that happened. There was a lot of beef and animosity before between most of us. Some things are not worth fighting.

Sheets’ death, like so many do, really seems to have put things in perspective for the rest of the cast. Their rivalries are what make the show so endlessly watchable, but in the end, they have known each other for almost two decades now, so something like this is bound to change things. Sheets’ manner of death is also a particularly difficult thing to endure, according to Passante:

I’ve endured a lot of deaths in that same manner over the years, and that is just a grief that, you know, kind of sticks with you. It’s not like losing somebody to cancer or a heart attack. It’s something that you think maybe you could have helped prevent. It’s one of those difficult deaths that you never can really wrap your head around.

Anyone who has lost a loved one to suicide knows how Passante feels. It can feel completely helpless. For her part, Passante is doing what she can, including checking in on Sheets’ son, Brandon, who was by his father’s side at all the auctions until Darrell left the show. Passante said:

I talk to [his son] Brandon a lot now. We didn’t really chat much over the years when they left. We would talk every once in a while during holidays or something, but now I just try to keep tabs. He sends me little messages maybe once a week. I just like to check in on him because it’s a hard thing to swallow. I’m sure that he’s missing his dad.

Ultimately, Passante summed it up quite succinctly by saying simply, “It sucks.”

There has been a lot of drama on Storage Wars over the years, and while much of it is contrived for the show, behind-the-scenes has been filled with drama, too. Passante has been in the middle of some of it when she divorced her long-time partner in life and in business, Jarrod Schulz, after Season 13 of the show. There has been nothing like the tragedy that befell Sheets, though, and keeping everything in perspective is important.

#3402. Steam Officially Launches Its 2026 Game of the Year Awards Voting

The Golden Joysticks has already weighed in on 2026's Game of the Year and The Game Awards has revealed its nominees for this year's best of the best. But one awards ceremony stands apart from the typical Game of the Year awards contest: the Steam Awards.

On Monday, Valve opened up nominations for its fan-voted awards, which include Game of the Year and what promises to be a highly contested category: the Hall of Fame Award. That brand-new category will pit a list of winners of the Steam Awards’ Game of the Year category from the past 10 years against each other to celebrate a decade of Valve's awards.

From now until Monday, Nov. 30 at 10 a.m. PST, Steam users can vote on the following categories, in addition to the Hall of Fame Award.

The final nominees will be revealed, and voting for the 2026 Steam Awards will begin, on Thursday, Dec. 17. That same day, the Steam Winter Sale kicks off. That's one week to the day after The Game Awards 2026, meaning that if any PC game was slighted by that awards ceremony, Steam users will have a chance to rebuke the TGAs voting body. (One thing that Steam Awards voters won't get to weigh in on is this year's GOTY frontrunner, Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar Games hasn't announced a PC version of the game yet.)

Last year's Steam Awards Game of the Year was Hollow Knight: Silksong. Other big winners from last year's Steam Awards include Baldur’s Gate 3, Hades 2, Peak, Silent Hill f, Arc Raiders, and Clair Obscur: Expedition 33.

#3401. Kate Middleton Announces Surprise Documentary About Her Cancer Journey

“Cancer does change you,” Kate Middleton says, emotion clear in her voice. “It changes your body, it changes you physically. But there’s a much, much deeper part to what a cancer diagnosis shifts in you.” These words come not at as an Instagram post or at a public event. Instead, they're the voice-over in a previously unannounced documentary about the Princess of Wales and her life since she disclosed a diagnosis of cancer in 2024.

According to Kensington Palace, which announced the film on Saturday, Heal is “a deeply personal new documentary from The Princess of Wales, exploring life beyond diagnosis and the many ways people find comfort, strength and hope in the face of serious illness.” It will air on the BBC in the UK on November 29, and in the US on NBCUniversal on November 30.

Heal follows Kate Middleton during her participation in one of the United Kingdom’s most demanding endurance events: The National Three Peaks Challenge, which she completed this summer. In less than 24 hours, the princess climbed the three highest mountains in Scotland, England, and Wales: Ben Nevis (4,413 feet), Scafell Pike (3,209 feet), and Yr Wyddfa–Snowdon (3,559 feet). The undertaking wasn't just a personal effort, as it was also in support of the Royal Marsden Cancer Charity, an organization that supports people living with cancer before, during, and after the disease.

The documentary will also support that organization, Kensington Palace notes, saying “All funds received through the documentary's distribution have been directed to The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity to help people living with and beyond cancer.” The Royal Marsden Hospital, at which Middleton received treatment, is also referenced in the film, as Middleton's brother, James, asks her “Isn’t it when you leave the Royal Marsden, you ring the bell?”

But while many patients participate in the bell-ringing ritual at the conclusion of treatment, Middleton says she missed out on that moment. “Yeah, but I didn’t ring the bell,” she replies. “So maybe this is your ringing of the bell,” James responded, suggesting her Three Peaks experience was that symbolic peal.

While Prince William is no stranger to documentary work, nor are Prince Harry and wife Meghan Markle, this is Kate Middleton's first venture into the format. Perhaps to ease her into the project, Heal's Director of Photography is a face quite familiar to the Princess: Will Warr, the filmmaker behind her video announcement marking the end of her chemotherapy treatments.

“Through this documentary, The Princess hopes to help others navigate diagnosis, recovery and life beyond cancer and transform access to holistic cancer care which supports wellbeing, resilience and quality of life during and after diagnosis,” Kensington Palace says of Heal, a message underscored by Middleton's words in the trailer. “You know, healing is a journey. How to reconnect with the things you once knew and how to find a sense of hope and joy alongside uncertainty.”

“It’s clear we're not meant to face life’s challenges alone,” the princess says as the trailer concludes. “Things can renew and grow. Often it is through pain that we realize that there is a greater beauty that lies beyond that."

#3400. 'Ghost Accounts' Are Putting Your Security at Risk, but You Can Protect Yourself

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

In all the years you've been online, you've likely created more accounts than you can remember, whether to shop on a website you made one purchase from, sign up for a newsletter you've since stopped reading, or download apps for school or work that you no longer need.

These so-called "ghost accounts"—all the old, forgotten logins that are still active but not in use—could expose your data in the event of a breach, increasing the risk of your information being used in malicious ways. That's why it's important to go through the effort to find and delete dormant accounts. Here's how to get started.

As McAfee describes, ghost accounts may retain lots of sensitive data, such as your contact details (phone numbers, emails, and addresses), purchase histories, payment details, and passwords. While this doesn't mean your information is sure to be compromised, the more places it lives, the more opportunities there are for bad actors to get ahold of it.

You're less likely to be keeping tabs on activity in older accounts, which may also have weak or reused passwords that haven't been updated in years. If that company or service experiences a data breach, not only is your stored data there exposed, but that information (including your password) can be used to access other accounts using tactics like credential stuffing and phishing. This also increases the risk of identity theft, as threat actors can use your name, birth date, and other information to open fraudulent accounts.

Unfortunately, finding and removing forgotten accounts can be tedious. If you have a password manager, the easiest way to start is to audit older items as well as look at security reports that identify weak or reused passwords, as well as data breaches that have impacted your accounts. If you've saved credentials in your browser keychain, go through the same process to find dormant accounts.

The next place to look is in your email: Search for account confirmation and verification emails as well as password resets using keywords like "verify your email," "free trial," "welcome," "confirm your account," or "sign up." Add a date filter to narrow down older accounts. Do this across all of your email addresses.

Once you've found accounts you no longer use, the next step is to deactivate or delete them, which you may be able to do through the settings or by reaching out to customer support. At the very least, remove all identifying information and change the password, and if possible, update the address to a burner using your browser's or password manager's hide-my-email feature. If you no longer have access to an old account, that doesn't mean it's been deactivated and your information removed, so you may need to reach out to customer support to find out how to access and delete it.

#3399. Steven Spielberg's Next Movie Is A Star-Studded Western Written By Another Legendary Filmmaker

Earlier this year, Steven Spielberg announced that his next movie as a director would be a Western. This will be his first official crack at the most American of film genres, and that's reason enough for cinephiles to get excited.

Now, Deadline has revealed that the movie, an adaptation of Kevin Barry's novel "The Heart in Winter," will star Cillian Murphy, Jessie Buckley and Mark Rylance, and it's hard not to be elated. Factor in that Barry's book is being adapted into a script by Oscar-winner Paul Thomas Anderson, and there isn't a word in the English language to capture the utter exhilaration movie fans are feeling at this moment.

No one's more enthused than Spielberg, though. As he told Deadline:

"It's really the excitement for me to get to work together with my dear friend and colleague Paul Thomas Anderson on a genre, but more particularly, the genre notwithstanding, a story that quite quickly became close to both our hearts and we felt that we could do as a team."

Murphy will play Tom Rourke, an Irish immigrant eking out a living in Butte, Montana. He works as an assistant to a photographer and supplements his income by penning letters for illiterate miners seeking potential brides from the east. He needs the extra scratch, too, due to his alcohol and opium addictions. Tom is spiritually adrift until mail-order bride Polly Gillespie arrives in Butte. They fall fast in love, steal some money, and set what proves to be an eventful course for San Francisco.

Overall, Barry's book has echoes of Spielberg's theatrical directing debut on "The Sugarland Express," as it's about two lovers on the run from the law. But this being the late 1800s, and the pair being challenged as horseback riders, their journey isn't quite as fast-paced.

Kevin Barry's "The Heart in Winter" has been described as "a tragedy written as farce" (per The Guardian). Critics found it hilarious and wildly entertaining, and after his excellent work on "One Battle After Another," I can't imagine anyone more suited to a tale about a character with an opium addiction stealing a mail-order bride and heading to San Francisco than Paul Thomas Anderson. But what's most interesting to me is that this will be the first time Anderson has written an entire script for another filmmaker. He previously did rewrites on the Apple-backed "Killers of the Flower Moon" and "Napoleon" for Martin Scorsese and Ridley Scott, but he's the primary writer here.

As for Steven Spielberg, no filmmaker alive knows more about Western conventions than him, and you can rest assured he will aggressively avoid cliché. I mean, he'll be sure to keep the horizon line out of the middle of the frame, lest John Ford's eye-patched ghost haunt him for the rest of his days, but don't expect traditional Western violence of the shootout and saloon brawl variety. I haven't read the book yet, so I don't know if such scenes exist in Barry's novel, but if they do, they'll look unlike any shootout or brawl you've ever seen.

What's curious is that Spielberg went with the Montana-set "The Heart in Winter," given that he'd been talking about making a Texas Western. Texas is not Montana by a long shot, which makes me wonder if he might change the location of Barry's novel. I doubt he'd do that, so now he's cheesed off everyone in Texas who was hoping he'd make their state look sensationally epic. He'll have to make it up to them somehow.

Could the original trio get back together?

Rupert Grint is the latest cast member from the Harry Potter films to join the Broadway run of Harry Potter and the Cursed Child, right on the heels of Tom Felton's successful run. With Ron Weasley in tow, he's already fielding questions about whether Emma Watson and Danielle Radcliffe could be next to join the stage play.

The actor, who will reprise his role as Ron for the production, confirmed it would be his last time playing the character. As such, Collider wanted to know if there was a chance of his former famous co-stars joining. Grint didn't say definitively one way or another, but offered up this:

It would be fun. I don't know. I mean, it's obviously different for everyone. It was an intense time. When we finished, I really enjoyed stepping away and not really even thinking about it, because it was such an intense… I mean, it was enjoyable, and they looked after us, but it was a big part of us. So, yeah, maybe. I don't know. It'd be fun.

I'm sure the last thing Grint wanted to do was try to put the pressure on Radcliffe and Watson to say no, knowing the complicated thoughts both may have about returning. Daniel Radcliffe has been pretty adamant about refusing any opportunities to return, and Emma Watson has shied away from acting so much that there were rumors a few years back that she had retired.

People are always free to change their minds of course, and Rupert Grint is evidence of that. He initially said he'd only return if everyone else did, and now he's in a position where he's being asked whether his co-stars will join him onstage for Harry Potter and the Cursed Child. He talked about his return and how he felt immediately after the film franchise ended way back when:

Yeah. It's funny. It's interesting, going back. I spent so much time after finishing Potter kind of moving away from it and doing other things, which I've really enjoyed doing, but I think now it's a very different role in a very different context. And weirdly, it's kind of lined up that I'm the exact age of the character in that story, so it's just felt like a good time.

It does feel like a good time, what with a new Harry Potter TV show on the way. The series' arrival on the 2026 TV schedule will likely spark even more interest than usual in the franchise, and possibly encourage a lot of millennials craving nostalgia to see Grint back as Ron.

Timing aside, I'm sure it doesn't surprise anyone that actors love to work. For Rupert Grint, the return to being on stage pulls back to his start as a child actor, and that's going to be a great joy for him:

And I love New York and being on stage. It's been a while since I've done that, and it's a very important thing to me. It was my childhood, and I have a very strong connection to that character and that world. I think I'm not going to get many other opportunities to play him again. It probably is my last, and I think it'll be fun.

It should be fun, especially given what Ron Weasley is up to in Harry Potter and the Cursed Child. He's running the joke shop Fred and George founded, while his wife Hermione is the literal Minister of Magic. As far as acting is concerned, it's more of a supportive role, but one that Rupert Grint will likely bring a special sparkle to.

I'm still waiting to see if Grint, Emma Watson, or Daniel Radcliffe will show up in the Potter TV series. Part of me thinks they'd do it for the fans, but at the same time, I could see them wanting the new cast to have a chance to do their own thing, without drawing attention to themselves. I guess all we can do is wait and see what happens!

Rupert Grint's run on Broadway in Harry Potter and the Cursed Child kicks off on February 2nd and will end on May 30th. I'm sure getting a ticket could be a struggle, but I'm eager to see what the demand will be for fans to see one of the core stars back in the franchise!

#3397. Miley Cyrus Marries Maxx Morando at Frank Sinatra's Famous Palm Springs Mansion

It's official: After more than five years together and nearly a year of engagement, Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando have tied the knot. The couple were married in the desert hot spot of Palm Springs, California on Saturday, November 21, an outdoor ceremony held at Frank Sinatra’s former mansion, with Wayne Coyne, frontman of The Flaming Lips and a Cyrus collaborator, officiating.

The 33-year-old singer and the 28-year-old musician—Morando is the drummer for the band Liily—had kept their plans a secret until Friday, when TMZ broke the news. Confirmation of the impending celebration emerged that same evening, during the dinner that capped off the rehearsal, when Miley’s half-sister, Lily-Rose Purcell, posted a photo on her Instagram Stories of a menu featuring the couple’s initials. This is Cyrus’s second marriage, following her alliance with actor Liam Hemsworth from 2018 to 2019.

Sinatra’s former home in Palm Springs, where the wedding took place

According to images published in outlets including People, the ceremony venue was decorated with white flowers and large candles, with Sinatra’s pool in the background. Miley Cyrus wore a long-sleeved white satin dress with a plunging back and no veil, while the groom opted for a classic black tuxedo with a bow tie.

Among the guests were the bride’s mother, Tish Cyrus, accompanied by her husband, actor Dominic Purcell, and Miley's sister, Noah Cyrus. Also in attendance was the singer’s father, Billy Ray Cyrus, along with his rumored fiancée, British actress Elizabeth Hurley, and her son, Damian.

Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando on February 01, 2026

As the bride has recounted in past interviews, her relationship with her now-husband began in 2021 following a blind date organized by mutual friends. That same year, they went public by attending the singer’s New Year’s Eve TV special in Miami together. Their engagement came to light in December 2025, when, during another of those joint appearances, Miley Cyrus posed on the red carpet wearing a diamond ring that turned out to be her engagement ring.

One of the most emotional moments of the ceremony took place just before the couple exchanged their vows, when—according to multiple outlets— Dolly Parton’s “Love Is Like a Butterfly” began to play. The nod follows a similar one Miley made last month, when she broke down in tears over Parton's death during a performance at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles.

“Me and Dolly, we are eternal. Nothing in this life could ever tear us apart, and I’m gonna see her again,” Cyrus told the stadium crowd in October, per The Hollywood Reporter. “And I can’t fucking wait because I miss her,” Cyrus tearfully continued. “Some of the greatest music that we have today was written, produced, performed by my Aunt Dolly."
